text:
alex_support: Heads-up — customer hit a big billing spike. They say our TypeScript/Node SDK is retrying immediately after AbortController aborts, and backoff values are ignored. Node 18.17, @redwood/sdk-js 0.9.4, undici 5.18. Logs pasted below.
rachel_eng: Can you paste the tiny repro and the raw logs? Need to confirm whether the SDK is passing the AbortSignal into the underlying fetch and whether the retry wrapper honors signal.aborted.
alex_support: Copying the snippet they used and a trimmed log. They use our responses API but this repro is generic:
```js
// repro.js
import Redwood from '@redwood/sdk';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, retries: 3, backoff: { initial: 100, factor: 2 } });
const ac = new AbortController();
setTimeout(() => ac.abort(), 1200);
try {
  await client.responses.create({ input: 'hi' , signal: ac.signal });
} catch (err) {
  console.error('call failed', err.name, err.message);
}
```
Logs (trimmed):
```
[2026-02-28T15:12:01.123Z] request -> 200ms -> CONNECT
[2026-02-28T15:12:02.350Z] retry #1 -> sending
[2026-02-28T15:12:02.352Z] fetch aborted: AbortError: The user aborted a request
[2026-02-28T15:12:02.353Z] retry #2 -> sending
[2026-02-28T15:12:02.354Z] billing: +0.20 USD
```
alex_support: Customer says they see a rapid sequence of retries after the AbortError; they expect abort to stop any further retries.
jess_repro: I ran that locally with same SDK and Node 18.17. Observed same behavior: the SDK's retry loop is implemented above the fetch call and does an immediate continue on network errors, but it doesn't check the AbortSignal between attempts. undici's fetch throws AbortError, which is caught and treated as transient; that's why we see extra retries.
jess_repro: Stack trace snippet:
```
Error: The user aborted a request
    at fetch (node:internal/fetch:xxx)
    at retryWrapper (/node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/request.js:45:12)
    at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues.js:93:5)
```
marcus_devex: Two things we can do for now:
1) Customer mitigation: set { retries: 0 } or call client.withOptions({ retries: 0 }) and add a short request timeout. That stops SDK-side retries immediately.
2) Short-term patch: SDK should check signal.aborted before each retry and pass the signal down into fetch. We should also avoid treating AbortError as transient.
marcus_devex: Example mitigation to send to the customer:
```js
// disable SDK retries for this flow
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, retries: 0 });
const ac = new AbortController();
setTimeout(() => ac.abort(), 1200);
await client.responses.create({ input: '…', signal: ac.signal, timeoutMs: 2000 });
```
rachel_eng: Agreed. I'll open a bug and patch the retry wrapper to:
- pass the AbortSignal to the underlying fetch
- if signal.aborted -> throw immediately (no retry)
- don't classify AbortError as retryable
I can target a fix for 0.9.5 and we can publish a short advisory.
tim_infra: One more note — Node 20 has an integrated undici, and users who mix a bundled undici with our pinned undici can end up with subtle differences in AbortError identity. Recommend reproducing on both Node 18 and Node 20 and verifying single undici instance used. If the customer uses a global fetch shim it could alter behavior.
alex_support: Thanks. Can you add the customer-facing text I can send right away?
rachel_eng: Send this to the customer:
"We've identified the issue: the SDK's retry loop currently doesn't respect AbortController signals. Short-term mitigation: set retries: 0 or disable retries for the call, or update your code to avoid mid-flight aborts while relying on SDK retries. We're releasing SDK patch 0.9.5 that fixes this (honors AbortSignal and won't retry after abort). If you need an immediate code change, use the snippet above. Also please try running under Node 20 or ensure there's only one undici version present if you still see odd behavior."
ci-bot: Deployment note: created cherry-pick branch fix/retry-abort-2026-03-01 (PR #1428) — scheduled for canary on staging.
alex_support: Perfect. Sending to customer now. Will follow up after they test the mitigation and once 0.9.5 is published.
